slides.headline: 7 repos from the most expensive engineering teams in the world.
slides.subtext: Jane Street. Goldman. JPMorgan. BlackRock. HRT. Two Sigma. D.E. Shaw.
slides.label: REAL INTERNAL TOOLS. OPEN SOURCE.
slides.note: Large headline. Firm names listed below in muted monospace. Label top-left in accent green. Swipe hint bottom-right.

slides.headline: When your profiler is blind, this sees every CPU instruction.
slides.body: Powered by Intel PT. Not sampling. Every instruction, in order, with exact timing.
slides.note: Tag top-left in green. Firm name + repo URL in monospace muted. Headline large. Body smaller below.

slides.headline: The derivative pricing library their traders use at their desks.
slides.body: Not a textbook. Working code. MIT licensed. You can run it today.
slides.note: Same layout as slide 2. Stars field shows license instead.

slides.headline: What JPM traders use to watch markets in real time. Free.
slides.body: Streaming data visualization. Handles tick-level data at scale. Maintained under FINOS.
slides.note: Stars field replaced with cost callout. Highlight 'Free.' in accent green.

slides.headline: Where scipy gives up, this works.
slides.body: Layered Conic Solver for Optimization. Portfolio problems at scale. BlackRock manages $10 trillion.
slides.note: Stars field shows language. '$10 trillion' in accent green or bold white.

slides.headline: The foundation of HFT infrastructure at one of the largest U.S. trading firms.
slides.body: Structured concurrency. Concurrent operations in a tree. Cancellation and error propagation that actually makes sense.
slides.note: Same layout. Language in stars slot.

slides.headline: Time-series joins when timestamps never match exactly.
slides.body: Tick data from different exchanges, different clocks. Temporal tolerance. Built for billions of ticks.

slides.headline: Auto-import for Jupyter. But read the footnote.
slides.body: D.E. Shaw funded IPython development. Every data scientist working in notebooks is using infrastructure they financed.
slides.note: Stars slot = 'Also funded IPython'. That's the hook. Bold the IPython line.

slides.headline: The algorithm is not the moat.
slides.body: The infrastructure that runs it reliably and fast enough is the moat. That's what every one of these repos shows.
slides.note: Full-bleed text slide. Headline large in white. Body in muted below. Minimal.

slides.headline: All 7 are public on GitHub.
slides.subtext: The README files alone are worth reading. Full breakdown at bionicbanker.tech
slides.cta: Follow for more from inside finance and AI.
